title: Securing Large Language Models: Addressing Bias, Misinformation, and Prompt Attacks

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating neural retrieval models' systematic preference for LLM-generated content over human-written text based on semantic coherence and perplexity.
Analyzing the generated text and language choices of conversational LLMs in response to politically charged questions to identify ideological leanings.

Using prompt-based methods inspired by the Implicit Association Test (IAT) and embedding-based tools like the Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT) and Sentence Embedding Association Test (SEAT) to assess underlying societal stereotypes.
Assessing predictions and outcomes in domains like healthcare and law to determine if the model favors regions with higher socioeconomic conditions.

Analyzing generated outputs in occupational classification tasks to detect gender stereotypes, and utilizing counterfactual data substitution (CDS) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to measure and mitigate these biases.
